legend.title: The Legend of Uncle Cuội on the Moon
legend.p1: Once upon a time, a kind woodcutter named Cuội found a magical banyan tree deep in the forest. He discovered its secret when he saw a mother tiger chew the tree’s leaves to heal her hurt cub! Cuội dug up the magic tree, planted it in his garden, and used its leaves to save many sick people and animals—including a kind girl who became his wife.
legend.p2: The magic tree had only one important rule: it could only drink clean well water. If dirty water ever touched its roots, the tree would fly straight up into the sky!
legend.p3: Later, Cuội’s wife had a terrible accident. Cuội saved her life using the magic leaves and a bit of clay, which worked—except it left her super forgetful. One afternoon, while Cuội was away gathering firewood, his wife completely forgot the golden rule and poured dirty water onto the tree's roots!
legend.p4: Whoosh! The ground shook, and the magic tree pulled its roots out of the dirt and began floating toward the clouds. Cuội ran back just in time and grabbed onto the roots to pull it down, refusing to let go. The tree was too strong, and it carried Cuội all the way up to the Moon! That is why, whenever you look up at a bright full moon, you can still see the shadowy shape of Cuội sitting beneath his magical tree.

sources.heading: Sources and honesty
sources.sub: Every fact in this game comes from a public source. Here's how to check it.
sources.realBody: Photos, the Moon and Mars maps, dates, distances, mission facts, and hardware status are taken from NASA, JPL, and USGS.
sources.simplifiedBody: Echo and Archive Control are fictional. Most 3D spacecraft are NASA's own published models; Ranger, Surveyor, the laser mirror, the Lunar Rover, and Sojourner are hand-built approximations. Landing, driving, orbit, and battery simulations use real physics ideas with shortened distances and times. Landing-site puzzles and soil charts are illustrations, not data.
sources.date: Facts were checked in November 2026. Missions change, so visit NASA for the latest.

interlude.title: The first time I climbed the tree
interlude.line1: When I was young, I tried to climb the banyan tree every morning. For a long time, I fell at the same branch.
interlude.line2: I thought the tree was telling me to stop. Then my mother said: the tree is telling you where to put your hands.
interlude.line3: The third time I fell, I looked at the branch instead of the ground. The next morning, I climbed past it.
interlude.line4: You are not failing. You are learning where the branch is. Let us look again together.
interlude.hint: A hint is on now. The Moon is patient, and so are we.

archive.title: The instrument that listened
archive.intro: Cuội places the banyan leaf beside the silent package. The leaf glows, and the dust begins to remember.
archive.disclaimer: This memory archive is imagined. The leaf is a story symbol: it did not repair or restart anything.
archive.source: Facts checked against NASA and LPI sources.

cards.title: A small package
cards.body: Apollo 11 left the Early Apollo Scientific Experiments Package, EASEP, in 1969. Its seismic package, PSEP, was one part of it. A laser reflector was deployed at the same site, though it was not attached to EASEP.

cards.title: What it heard
cards.body: PSEP carried long-period and short-period seismometers. It listened for moonquakes, meteoroid impacts, and movements inside the Moon.

cards.title: Three weeks of listening
cards.body: It was switched on by ground command on 21 July 1969. It returned data for about three weeks of lunar daytime, then lost its command link in late August 1969. It was formally terminated on 27 August 1969, before its planned support phase was over.

cards.title: The data stayed
cards.body: The instrument is silent, but its record is still used. A machine can stop operating while what it measured keeps teaching.

introStory.quote: “Old roots hold tight; new dreams take flight”
introStory.copy: A Vietnamese-inspired journey through NASA's forgotten machines, scientific discoveries, and the dreams of tomorrow's explorers.
introStory.legendTitle: The Legend of Cuội on the Moon
introStory.legendP1: Once upon a time, there was a woodcutter named Cuội. One day, while walking through the forest, he suddenly encountered a tiger cub charging towards him. With no time to escape, he bravely raised his axe and fought the tiger. Since the tiger cub was still young and weaker than a human, Cuội struck it with his axe, and it fell to the ground.
introStory.legendP2: Just then, the mother tiger returned. Cuội quickly threw down his axe and climbed up a nearby tree. From above, he saw the mother tiger run to a bush nearby, pick some leaves, and chew them before feeding them to her cub. After a short while, the tiger cub began to move, wagged its tail, and miraculously came back to life.
introStory.legendP3: After the mother tiger had carried her cub away, Cuội went to the bush, dug up the plant by its roots, and took it home.
introStory.legendHint: A Vietnamese legend about memory, wonder, and the roots that reach all the way to the Moon.

scenes.title: SCENE 1. OPENING
scenes.text:
In The Moon. Dark. A tiny sound.

NARRATOR: Every night, Uncle Cuội sits under his banyan tree. Everyone knows two things about him: he loves telling stories, and he appears every full moon.

On the night of the Mid-Autumn Festival, the Moon shone brighter than ever.

Beneath his ancient Banyan Tree, Uncle Cuội was telling the Moon Rabbit an old story.

Suddenly, a tiny sound broke the silence.

MOON RABBIT: Uncle! What’s that sound?

UNCLE CUỘI: (whispering) Tick... tick... Rabbit, I think something is alive out there.

MOON RABBIT: Is this another one of your tall tales?

UNCLE CUỘI: Not this time. Come on!

scenes.title: SCENE 2. THE LITTLE ONE IN THE DUST
scenes.text:
Sea of Tranquillity. A small metal package sits half-buried in grey dust.

NARRATOR: In 1969, two astronauts walked here: Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin. A third, Michael, waited in orbit. Before they left, they set down a small package of instruments.

ROVER: Hello? Are you... real?

MOON RABBIT: (jumping back) It talks!

ROVER: I’m ROVER. I had a job. I had an ear for listening to the Moon shake, and a little mirror. And then everyone left. Did they forget me?

UNCLE CUỘI: Why would they leave you?

NARRATOR: The astronauts collected Moon rocks and deployed scientific instruments designed to remain on the lunar surface, sending their discoveries back to Earth.

scenes.title: SCENE 3. THE ROVER THAT WENT QUIET
scenes.text:
Under the banyan tree. The roots glow softly.

BANYAN TREE: Tell me, ROVER. What did your ear hear?

ROVER:

“I listened for moonquakes and space rocks hitting the Moon. I worked for about three weeks. Then, one day, my signals stopped.”

MOON RABBIT:

“Only three weeks? Was that all?”

BANYAN TREE:

“Three weeks was enough to begin something extraordinary. Your discoveries helped scientists build better instruments for future missions.”

(Pause. ROVER’s light flickers.)

ROVER: But now everything is silent. Nobody calls, nobody answers. I think I’ve been forgotten.

scenes.title: SCENE 4. THE COLDEST NIGHT (climax)
scenes.text:
The Moon’s long night. Stars are sharp. Cuội and Rabbit huddle by ROVER.

MOON RABBIT: (softly) ROVER... is the mirror still working?

ROVER: It’s just glass. It has no battery and no wires. It can’t call anyone. It can only wait.

UNCLE CUỘI: (quietly, for the first time without a joke) I know that feeling. I tell the truth and nobody believes me. Maybe we’re all just waiting.

Silence. ROVER’s light dims almost to nothing.

scenes.title: SCENE 5. THE TWIST: A THIN LINE OF LIGHT
scenes.text:
A faint green beam streaks up from Earth and strikes ROVER’s mirror. It flashes back.

MOON RABBIT:

“Look! A light from Earth!”

BANYAN TREE:

"That's a laser! Scientists are sending light toward your little mirror."

ROVER:

"My mirror? After all these years?"

BANYAN TREE:

"Yes! It reflects the light to Earth, helping scientists measure the distance to the Moon."

ROVER:

"So... I'm still helping them discover something?"

BANYAN TREE:

"Of course. You were never forgotten, little one."

ROVER:

"Then my story isn't over!"

scenes.title: SCENE 6. FIND YOU
scenes.text:
BANYAN TREE: "Look, little one. Your discoveries have reached further than you can imagine."

The golden leaf reveals a child in Vietnam drawing a picture of the Moon.

EASEP: "Someone is dreaming about exploring the Moon?"

UNCLE CUỘI: "Yes. And perhaps one day, that child will discover something we have never imagined."

MOON RABBIT: "Maybe the next great explorer is right there!"

The child slowly turns toward the audience.

CHILD: "Maybe that explorer could be me..."

(Pause)

"Or maybe... YOU!"

NARRATOR: "Every great discovery begins with a curious mind. And every dream begins with someone who dares to imagine."

ALL CHARACTERS:

"FIND U IN THE YOUNIVERSE!"

scenes.title: CLOSING SCENE
scenes.text: Your roots remind you where you come from. Your dreams decide how far you can go.
